title: History-Dependent Recursive Preferences in Markov Decision Processes
summary: In finite horizon dynamic programming with history-dependent preferences, the relevant state may be the entire realized history, even when the physical state is Markov. This paper develops a behavioral state-reduction theory for such Markov decision processes. Under behavioral axioms and a certainty-equivalent richness condition, the full-history problem admits a recursive representation composed of time and risk aggregators.
